sections.content: How many people stayed in Brighton and Hove after gaining qualifications?

Brighton and Hove is a city in the South East. Brighton and Hove also has a university.

Brighton and Hove has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Brighton and Hove ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 7,050 state-school pupils from Brighton and Hove who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,210 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,115 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Brighton and Hove to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Brighton and Hove's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Brighton and Hove in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Brighton and Hove move to?

Of Brighton and Hove's graduates, 810 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those graduates (8%) were living fairly locally, in the Brighton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Brighton and Hove's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 530 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 115 of those qualified non-graduates (22%) were living fairly locally, in the Brighton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Brighton and Hove's GCSE cohort:

  • 570 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 200 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 70% of graduates and 51% of qualified non-graduates living in Brighton and Hove had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 4,460 graduates and 3,175 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Brighton and Hove. This is compared with the 2,210 graduates and 2,115 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 30% of the graduates had also lived in Brighton and Hove as GCSE pupils, while 70% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Brighton and Hove in 2018 to 2019, 49% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 51% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
